experience.title: Experience Ancient Split Through Virtual Reality
experience.p1: Diocletian's Dream is a 15-minute virtual reality experience a few steps from Diocletian's Palace in Split. It rebuilds the palace complex in 3D and shows you the whole thing as it stood in 305 AD.
experience.p2: You stand inside rooms that no longer survive in their original form and watch scenes drawn from the historical record. Few visitors ever get to see the palace at the height of Diocletian's reign. This is the closest you can get.
experience.p3: The reconstruction is built around atmosphere and scale. You come away understanding how the palace worked around the emperor, and how the city of Split later grew inside its walls.

authority.title: A reconstruction grounded in scholarship
authority.copy: Expert historical insight shaped how we interpreted Diocletian's Palace as it stood in 305 AD, from its architecture and proportions down to the atmosphere of daily life inside the imperial complex.
authority.detail: Historical and artistic research guides the whole experience, so the technology serves the story instead of replacing it.

story.title: The Story Behind Diocletian's Dream
story.p1: Diocletian's Dream was created to present cultural heritage in a way modern audiences actually engage with. The project pairs historical research with virtual reality to give Roman architecture a form you can walk through.
story.p2: It is Croatia's leading virtual reality heritage experience, built to connect today's visitors with ancient history.

faq.title: Frequently Asked Questions
faq.text: Everything you need to know before your visit: how long the experience takes, what it costs, booking, age suitability, and how to find us.

duration.a: The VR museum experience lasts about 15 minutes and you stay seated throughout. Plan on roughly 25 minutes at the venue in total, which covers the short staff briefing before your session and time to get the headset comfortable.

price.q: How much does a ticket cost?
price.a: An adult ticket is €13 and a child ticket, for ages 8 to 14, is €9. That is the full price for one 15-minute session. You can pay online when you book or at the door when a session still has space.

booking.q: Do I need to book in advance?
booking.a: Booking ahead is the safest way to get the time slot you want. Each session holds a limited number of visitors and slots fill up quickly in July and August. We do take walk-ins whenever a session still has room.

age.a: Yes, for visitors aged 8 and over. Children under 8 cannot take part, because the headsets do not fit smaller heads safely and the 360-degree format is a lot for younger children. Under-14s should come with an adult.

location.a: We are at Zagrebačka ul. 1, just outside the palace walls beside the Golden Gate. It is under a minute on foot from the palace complex, so most visitors do the VR experience either right before or right after walking the site.

language.q: What languages is the experience available in?
language.a: The narration runs in eight languages: English, German, Italian, French, Croatian, Spanish, Portuguese and Polish. You pick yours before the session starts, and everyone in a session can choose independently.

firstTime.q: Do I need any experience with VR headsets?
firstTime.a: No. Most of our visitors have never worn a VR headset before. Our staff fit the headset for you, explain what to expect, and stay in the room for the whole session. There is nothing to operate: you sit, look around, and the story comes to you.

worthIt.q: Is it worth doing if I have already walked around the palace?
worthIt.a: That is when it works best. Walking the palace today means seeing medieval and modern buildings grown into a Roman shell. The VR reconstruction strips those centuries away and shows you the volumes and rooflines that the surviving walls only hint at.

howItWorks.title: How the Experience Works
howItWorks.p1: The VR experience lasts about 15 minutes.
howItWorks.p2: Sessions run every 30 minutes through the day at fixed times, on the hour and half past: 11:00, 11:30, 12:00, 12:30 and so on. Arrive a few minutes before your slot so your session starts on time. The last session of the day begins 30 minutes before closing.
howItWorks.p3: Our staff give you a short introduction, fit your headset, and guide you into the reconstructed palace. The whole thing is built for first-time VR users, and there are no controllers to learn.
howItWorks.p4: Visitors go in as small groups at their assigned time. For opening hours and practical planning, see Visit Us.

accuracy.title: Historical Reconstruction and Accuracy
accuracy.p1: The digital reconstruction is built on archaeological research, historical sources and architectural analysis of what survives of the palace. Where the original structures are only partly preserved today, the VR experience completes them visually. The point is to give you historical context you can stand inside instead of an abstract explanation.

items.q: How long does the experience last?
items.a: The VR experience lasts about 15 minutes. Sessions start every 30 minutes, on the hour and half past, so 11:00, 11:30, 12:00 and onward. Arrive a few minutes early for your slot. The final screening begins 30 minutes before closing time.

items.q: Is it suitable for children?
items.a:
The experience is suitable for children aged 8 and above. Younger visitors cannot take part, and under-14s should be accompanied by an adult.

This is a fully immersive 360-degree virtual reality experience, so participants should be comfortable wearing a headset and being inside a digital environment. Anyone sensitive to motion simulation, virtual heights or intense visual effects may want to weigh that up first.

If you are unsure, ask our staff before the session and they will talk you through it.

items.q: Do I need to book in advance?
items.a: Advance booking is recommended, especially in peak season. You can secure your time slot on the Book Now page.

items.q: Is the experience physically demanding?
items.a: No. The whole experience is seated. You stay comfortably in your chair for the full 15 minutes and turn your head to look around. There is no walking, no standing and nothing to hold.

items.q: What will I actually see inside the headset?
items.a: You see Diocletian's Palace rebuilt at full architectural scale in 305 AD. That covers the ceremonial and residential rooms that no longer survive, the colonnaded spaces of the imperial complex, and the harbour that served the emperor's household. The reconstruction follows archaeological research and architectural analysis of the surviving remains.

items.q: Which languages is the narration available in?
items.a: Eight: English, German, Italian, French, Croatian, Spanish, Portuguese and Polish. You choose before your session begins, and each visitor in the same session can pick a different one, so mixed groups do not have to agree on a single language.

items.q: Will virtual reality make me feel motion sick?
items.a: Most visitors are fine, because the experience is seated and the camera moves gently instead of throwing you around. If you know you are sensitive to motion simulation or virtual heights, tell our staff before you start. You can stop and take the headset off at any point in the session.

items.q: How early should I arrive for my session?
items.a: A few minutes before your slot is enough. Sessions run on fixed 30-minute intervals and start on time, so arriving five minutes early leaves room for the staff briefing and for getting the headset fitted comfortably before the reconstruction begins.

items.q: Is the venue wheelchair accessible?
items.a: Yes. Diocletian's Dream is on the ground floor at Zagrebačka ul. 1, with step-free access from the street. The experience itself is seated, so it works from a wheelchair. Let us know when you book if you would like staff to help with the transfer.

items.q: How historically accurate is the reconstruction?
items.a: The model is built from archaeological research, historical sources and architectural analysis of the palace remains. Where the surviving structures are incomplete, the reconstruction fills the gaps with the most defensible interpretation instead of a guess. Professor Josip Belamarić advised on the historical interpretation.

hero.title: About Diocletian's Dream
hero.p1: Diocletian's Dream is a virtual reality heritage experience and VR museum in the historic centre of Split, Croatia. It presents Diocletian's Palace through immersive 3D reconstruction, and it was built by combining archaeological interpretation, architectural analysis and current VR technology.
hero.p2: It was one of the first dedicated virtual reality museum concepts in Croatia and remains a distinct cultural experience inside Split's UNESCO-listed Old Town.

mission.title: Our Mission
mission.p1: Diocletian's Dream exists to give visitors a clearer spatial understanding of Diocletian's Palace as it appeared in 305 AD.
mission.p2: The palace is one of the most significant Roman monuments in the world, but centuries of adaptation and urban development changed most of its original structure. The VR reconstruction shows the palace's architectural scale, its ceremonial spaces and its imperial layout as a single coherent building again.
mission.p3: The experience complements traditional historical interpretation instead of replacing it, so visitors can make sense of what they see in the surviving remains.
mission.linkSentence: Learn more about how the reconstruction works on our Experience page.

whyVr.title: Why Virtual Reality and History
whyVr.p1: Historical sites ask a lot of your imagination. Walls survive, volumes disappear. Structures fragment, and their original proportions get hard to read.
whyVr.p2: Virtual reality changes what a visitor can do with a ruin. Rebuilding architectural environments at full scale lets you understand:
whyVr.p3: Through 360-degree modelling, Diocletian's Dream presents the palace as one integrated architectural system inside the Roman Empire.

origin.title: The Origin of the Project
origin.p1: The idea behind Diocletian's Dream came from a simple observation: even guided tours of Diocletian's Palace lean heavily on explanation and imagination.
origin.p2: Walking through the palace today means mentally rebuilding it as you go. Diocletian's Dream was developed to close that gap, using digital technology in service of historical interpretation. The founders wanted a space where visitors could step out of the crowded streets, sit down, and see a complete architectural reading of the imperial residence.
origin.p3: Development took over a year and brought together historians, designers, digital artists and VR specialists. The experience opened to the public in 2020 and has since welcomed tens of thousands of visitors.
origin.p4: From April 2026, visitors can see a completely new VR film, produced to current immersive technology standards, with better visual quality and more narrative depth than the original reconstruction.

languages.title: Available in Multiple Languages
languages.p1: To keep the experience open to international visitors, Diocletian's Dream runs in eight languages: English, German, Italian, French, Croatian, Spanish, Portuguese and Polish.
languages.p2: The goal has always been to present Roman heritage clearly across different cultural backgrounds. Multilingual narration lets visitors engage with the historical reconstruction in the language they think in.

media.title: Media and Public Recognition
media.p1: Since opening, Diocletian's Dream has been featured in regional and international travel publications, cultural portals and news outlets.
media.p2: Coverage has described the experience as a new approach to Roman heritage, a modern complement to walking tours of Split, and a distinctive indoor cultural activity inside the Old Town.

items.q: What is Diocletian's Dream?
items.a: Diocletian's Dream is a virtual reality museum in Split, Croatia. It runs a 15-minute seated VR experience that rebuilds Diocletian's Palace as it stood in 305 AD, at full architectural scale, from archaeological research and architectural analysis of the surviving remains.

items.q: Is Diocletian's Dream a real museum?
items.a: It is a VR museum, so there is no collection of artefacts. Instead of display cases, the exhibit is the palace itself, digitally rebuilt and presented in 360 degrees. It was one of the first dedicated virtual reality museum concepts in Croatia when it opened in 2020.

items.q: When did Diocletian's Dream open?
items.a: Diocletian's Dream opened to the public in 2020, after more than a year of development involving historians, designers, digital artists and VR specialists. Tens of thousands of visitors have been through it since, and it won the Tripadvisor Travellers' Choice award in 2022 and 2023.

items.q: How was the reconstruction researched?
items.a: The model is based on archaeological research, historical sources and architectural analysis of the palace remains. Professor Josip Belamarić advised on the historical interpretation, from the architecture and proportions of the complex down to how daily life inside it would have looked.

items.q: Is Diocletian's Dream inside Diocletian's Palace?
items.a: We are just outside the palace walls, at Zagrebačka ul. 1, about a minute on foot from the Golden Gate entrance. The whole area sits inside Split's UNESCO World Heritage zone, so you are within the historic core either way.

items.q: What changes with the new VR film in April 2026?
items.a: From April 2026 the experience runs a completely new VR film, produced to current immersive technology standards. It improves visual quality and adds narrative depth compared with the original 2020 reconstruction. The format stays the same: 15 minutes, seated, sessions every 30 minutes.

items.a: We are at Zagrebačka ul. 1, just outside the walls of Diocletian's Palace near the Golden Gate. The venue is fully indoor and wheelchair accessible, with step-free access from the street.

items.q: Can I buy tickets on arrival?
items.a: Yes, walk-in visitors are welcome whenever a session still has room. Because sessions run in fixed time slots with limited seating, we strongly recommend booking in advance. If your preferred slot is already full when you arrive, our staff will offer you the next available session.

items.q: Can I change or cancel my booking?
items.a: You can reschedule or cancel free of charge up to 24 hours before your session. Inside that 24-hour window, contact us directly and we will help where we can. If a technical problem stops your session going ahead, you get a full refund or another time slot.

items.q: Is there a minimum age?
items.a: Yes. The experience is for visitors aged 8 and above, and children under 8 cannot take part. Under-14s should be accompanied by an adult. If tickets are bought for a child below the minimum age, entry may be declined on arrival without a refund.

items.q: In which languages is the experience available?
items.a: The VR experience runs in English, German, Italian, French, Croatian, Spanish, Polish and Portuguese. You choose your language before the session begins, and each visitor in a session can pick a different one.

items.q: Do you offer group or school rates?
items.a: Yes. Discounted rates are available for school groups, with pricing based on the number of students and the group size. Organised travel groups and private bookings are quoted separately. Contact us ahead of your visit for a tailored offer and available dates.
